title: Persistent Log-Structured Message Broker in Go with Segmented Storage, Consumer Groups & At-Least-Once Delivery
problem: Relying on external message brokers without understanding their underlying storage and replication mechanics leads to silent message loss, consumer partition starvation, and runaway disk exhaustion. In-memory queues lack crash durability, while naive file-based queues suffer from catastrophic disk write bottlenecks when executing synchronous disk syncs per message. This project builds a production-grade persistent message queue and log broker from scratch in Go. The system implements append-only log segmentation with index files, manages consumer group partition assignment and offset commits, guarantees at-least-once delivery with unacknowledged message redelivery timeouts, and isolates unprocessable poisoned messages into dead-letter queues.

use_cases.title: Asynchronous E-Commerce Order Fulfillment Pipelines
use_cases.first_sentence: E-commerce checkout platforms need durable message buffering to decouple instant client checkout confirmations from downstream payment and shipping services.
use_cases.second_sentence: The broker persists order messages to disk logs, ensuring that even if backend inventory workers crash, all pending orders are reliably redelivered and processed.

use_cases.title: Financial Transaction Audit Event Streaming
use_cases.first_sentence: Core banking and payment processing services require immutable, sequentially ordered audit records for every account debit and credit transaction.
use_cases.second_sentence: The engine writes transactions to sequential segmented log files with binary index offsets, guaranteeing deterministic replayability and non-repudiation.

use_cases.title: High-Volume Telemetry and IoT Ingestion Buffering
use_cases.first_sentence: Smart device fleet management systems ingest millions of sensor status pings per minute that fluctuate wildly during peak operational hours.
use_cases.second_sentence: The queue absorbs high-concurrency ingestion bursts using batched memory buffers and sequential append-only writes without dropping packets.

hard_parts: Designing a high-performance binary log segment format with sparse indexing for fast message offset lookups
Coordinating consumer group partition assignments and cooperative rebalancing upon worker member joins or leaves
Implementing reliable at-least-once delivery with acknowledgement timeout tracking and dead-letter queue routing
Balancing write throughput and data durability using batching windows and controlled fsync disk flushing
screener_signals: Clean idiomatic Go codebase implementing binary file protocol serialization, segment rotation, and consumer offset stores
High-throughput benchmark report validating 45,000+ messages per second sustained ingestion with crash durability
Anti-fake verification script simulating consumer worker crash mid-batch and asserting broker redelivers unacknowledged messages to surviving consumer

components.name: Custom Binary TCP Wire Protocol Server
components.purpose: Parses incoming binary framing packets for Produce, Fetch, Commit, and Heartbeat commands

components.name: Append-Only Segmented Log Storage Engine
components.purpose: Appends messages to active log segment files, maintains sparse index offsets, and rotates segments at size limits

components.name: Consumer Group & Partition Offset Coordinator
components.purpose: Manages consumer group memberships, tracks committed partition offsets, and coordinates rebalancing

components.name: Acknowledgement Tracker & Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ)
components.purpose: Tracks unacknowledged in-flight message leases, triggers redelivery on timeout, and routes poisoned records to DLQ

architecture.data_flow: Producers connect over TCP and emit binary Produce requests containing topic, partition, and payload; the log engine writes messages to the active binary segment file and updates the sparse index file; periodic or threshold-based fsync calls commit data to durable disk; consumer group workers connect and issue Fetch requests with current partition offsets; the broker returns message batches and starts an unacknowledged lease timer; when consumers emit Commit requests, the offset advances in the metadata store; if a consumer crashes before committing, the lease expires and the broker redelivers unacknowledged messages to an active consumer; messages failing 3 redeliveries divert to the dead-letter queue topic.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Append-only immutable file writes preventing data corruption; CRC32 checksums on every message payload verifying integrity.

prerequisites: Proficiency in Go systems programming, binary encoding (binary.Read/Write), and goroutine concurrency
Understanding of file system I/O (os.File, mmap, fsync) and distributed messaging semantics

environment.gpu: None required (purely CPU and storage I/O bound systems software)
environment.accounts_keys_quotas: No external cloud accounts, paid services, or API keys required
environment.reference_environment: Local 4-core CPU with Go 1.21+ and local SSD storage
environment.fallback_path: Pure standard library Go binary running on local disk without external dependencies

riskiest_component.name: File System Disk Write Bottlenecks on Synchronous fsync Calls
riskiest_component.mitigation: Implement group commit batching (flushing every N messages or M milliseconds) and pre-allocate segment files.
riskiest_component.fallback: Configurable asynchronous write mode with background sync goroutine.

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: a persistent log-structured message broker in Go with segmented storage, consumer groups, and at-least-once delivery.
worksheet.q2: Target users: distributed systems developers, data infrastructure engineers, and backend platform architects.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: e-commerce order fulfillment buffering, financial transaction audit event streaming, and IoT telemetry ingestion.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 28 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 24 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 27.6 -> 28 hours. Intermediate level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: binary log segment framing with sparse index lookups, consumer group partition rebalancing, at-least-once delivery with lease timeouts, and fsync batching.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: binary framing protocol spec, consumer group mock harness, and 50,000 synthetic message payloads. Synthetic payloads only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: local disk file operations without Docker.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: synchronous fsync bottlenecks. Fallback: group commit batching and pre-allocated segment files.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: in-memory mock queues. Anti-fake check 5 crashes worker during dynamic publish, asserts surviving consumer receives redelivered message.
worksheet.q10: Safety/ethics: Safe; local loopback binary TCP and synthetic payloads only, zero production infrastructure exposure.
